g_policy.reason: The banner is opt-in, the offer copy states the reward (30 minutes with no sponsored stories), declining changes nothing, and 'if the ad fails' covers both a missing game and an unconfirmed play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes without sponsored cards, a feature_time reward that has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an article-open counter reaching 3 and a return to the feed, which are app events and involve no user-typed content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed, locked or capped. Feed, articles, saving and sharing stay as they are, and the reward only adds a temporary ad-free window.

g_brand_safety.reason: The banner is a card in the feed chrome on s01, which is rated safe. It is not in a conversation and not next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: As a product_change, the new ad-free reading window is tied to the observed read-a-story loop (f01, s01 to s02) and the sponsored cards it hides (s01.e44, s02.e13).

c2_evidence.reason: The proposal claims AOL shows a full-screen video ad after every third article, and nothing in the product model supports it. The model lists only native Taboola cards and an s05 in-article ad, so this claim rests on something unobserved.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No paid plan or subscription was observed, and the reward is a 30-minute limited window, so no subscription benefit is given away.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears when the reader returns to the feed after finishing an article, which is a finished-action moment, and never in the middle of reading.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn unit, the reward is granted only once the play is confirmed, and the trigger is a detectable article-open counter.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names concrete elements of this app: the Taboola card below the first story on s01, the in-article card on s02, and the read-a-story loop.

other_concern: Hiding the app's own Taboola cards may cost the publisher revenue, and the model does not show whether the ad slots can be suppressed per session. The 'North American audience' remark is speculation. The unsupported AOL full-screen claim also weakens the rationale that the hidden cards are low-value.
